title: Toyota 4Runner Engines by Year (1984–2026)
description: Every factory engine in the Toyota 4Runner by year, 1984–2026: the 22R fours, 3VZ and 5VZ V6s, the 4.0 V6 and 4.7 V8, and the turbo four and hybrid of the newest model.
intro: Toyota's 4Runner began in 1984 as a pickup-based SUV and is now in its sixth generation. The engine codes Toyota uses (22R-E, 5VZ-FE, 1GR-FE) are shown with each engine.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first 4Runner used the 22R four, fuel-injected as the 22R-E from 1985 and turbocharged as the 22R-TE for 1986–1987, and the 3.0 3VZ-E V6 from 1988.
The 4.0 1GR-FE V6 and the 4.7 2UZ-FE V8. The 2006 ratings are lower because of a change in the SAE test, not the engines.
The 1GR-FE V6, with a 2.7 four in 2010 two-wheel-drive models.
The current 4Runner uses a 2.4 turbo four, alone or as the i-FORCE MAX hybrid. The hybrid's rating is the combined output of engine and motor.

excluded.researchNote: Hagerty says the 22R-E was 'offered as an option' for 1985, implying the carbureted 22R stayed as base; Wikipedia lists the 22R for 1984 only. EPA lists only '2.4 L 4-cyl' and cannot tell them apart. Not confirmed; hp withheld (96 vs 100).

excluded.name: 2.7L / 164 inline-four
excluded.researchNote: EPA lists a 2011 4Runner 2WD 2.7 L 4-cyl, but Cars.com's 2011 trim list is V6-only and Wikipedia/CarGurus say the I4 lasted one year (2010). Probably an EPA certification carryover; do not publish.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
